nyciml-2021-22-spring-seniorb-01.title: Fraction of triangle area
nyciml-2021-22-spring-seniorb-01.body: Triangle $ABC$ is right ($15^2+20^2=25^2$) with area $\tfrac{1}{2}(15)(20)=150$. The 4 equally spaced points divide $BC$ into 5 equal parts, creating a grid of small congruent triangles (all similar to $\triangle ABC$). The shaded region consists of 6.5 parallelogram-equivalents out of 12.5 total, giving fraction $\tfrac{13}{25}$. Shaded area $=\tfrac{13}{25}\cdot150=78$. **Answer: 78**

nyciml-2021-22-spring-seniorb-02.title: f(x) multiplies by a prime
nyciml-2021-22-spring-seniorb-02.body: For 1-digit $x$: $f(x)=11x$, and 11 is prime and cannot divide $x<10$. For 2-digit $x$: $f(x)=101x$, and 101 is prime and cannot divide $x<100$. So in each case $f(x)=px$ where $p$ is prime and $\gcd(p,x)=1$. Every divisor $d$ of $x$ gives divisors $d$ and $pd$ of $f(x)$, exactly doubling the count. All 49 positive integers less than 50 satisfy the condition. **Answer: 49**

nyciml-2021-22-spring-seniorb-03.title: Equality at a=b=c
nyciml-2021-22-spring-seniorb-03.body: $(a+b+c)^2=a^2+b^2+c^2+2(ab+bc+ca)=81$, so $ab+bc+ca=\tfrac{81-(a^2+b^2+c^2)}{2}$. This is maximized when $a^2+b^2+c^2$ is minimized, which by convexity occurs at $a=b=c=3$, giving $ab+bc+ca=27$. **Answer: 27**

nyciml-2021-22-spring-seniorb-04.title: 30-60-90 triangle from A
nyciml-2021-22-spring-seniorb-04.body: Let $P$ be the foot of the perpendicular from $A$ to $FE$. Triangle $AFP$ is $30°$-$60°$-$90°$ with $\angle FAP=30°$, $AP=\sqrt{3}\cdot FA/2$. Triangle $AEP$ is also $30°$-$60°$-$90°$ with $AE=2AP$. The sum of perpendicular lengths $AP+AE_{\perp}=AP+2AP=3AP=3\sqrt{3}$, so $AP=\sqrt{3}$ and $FA=2$. Area of regular hexagon with side 2: $6\cdot\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{4}(4)=6\sqrt{3}$. **Answer: $6\sqrt{3}$**

nyciml-2021-22-spring-seniorb-05.title: Find first 3 consecutive representable numbers
nyciml-2021-22-spring-seniorb-05.body: Check small values: 3, 7, 8 are representable; 6=3+3, 7, 8 are three consecutive representable numbers. Any number $\ge6$ can be obtained by adding multiples of 3. Check 5: $5=a\cdot3+b\cdot7+c\cdot8$ has no non-negative integer solution. So 5 is the largest non-representable number. **Answer: 5**

nyciml-2021-22-spring-seniorb-06.title: Stars and bars bijection
nyciml-2021-22-spring-seniorb-06.body: Set up a bijection between valid numbers and arrangements of 7 stars and 5 bars: the number of stars to the right of each bar encodes the digits, with $+1$ added for the $A$ and $C$ positions to enforce strict inequalities. This gives $\binom{12}{5}=792$ arrangements. **Answer: 792**

nyciml-2021-22-spring-seniorb-07.title: Add inequalities
nyciml-2021-22-spring-seniorb-07.body: Adding the first and second constraints: $a+2b+c\le9$, so $a+b+c\le9-b\le9$. This upper bound is achieved by $a=6,b=0,c=3,d=0$, which satisfies all constraints. **Answer: 9**

nyciml-2021-22-spring-seniorb-08.title: Choose which go in one group
nyciml-2021-22-spring-seniorb-08.body: Label the 4 people 1, 2, 3, 4 by increasing height. Each partition into two non-empty groups has a unique height-sorted order within each group. Fix person 1 in one group to avoid counting unordered pairs twice. Each of persons 2, 3, 4 either joins person 1's group or the other group; the other group must be non-empty. This gives $2^3-1=7$ assignments. **Answer: 7**

nyciml-2021-22-spring-seniorb-10.title: Similar triangles and area ratios
nyciml-2021-22-spring-seniorb-10.body: Let $AB=x$; $CD=5x$, $DE=3x$, $EC=2x$. Since $AB\parallel CD$, $\triangle FAB\sim\triangle FDE$ with ratio $1:3$, so $[FDE]=9[FAB]=81$ and $[ABED]=[FDE]-[FAB]=72$. Trapezoids $ABED$ and $BCEA$ share height; ratio of areas $=(3+1)x:(2+1)x=4:3$. So $[BCEA]=54$. $\triangle GAB\sim\triangle GEC$ with ratio $1:2$; $[GAB]:[ABCE]=1:3$, so $[GAB]=54/3=18$. **Answer: 18**

nyciml-2021-22-spring-seniorb-11.title: Rearrange into half a square
nyciml-2021-22-spring-seniorb-11.body: Cut the figure along $CO_1$; paste the left half so $A$ coincides with $B$. The shaded region forms exactly half of a $6\times6$ square. Area $=\tfrac{36}{2}=18$. **Answer: 18**

nyciml-2021-22-spring-seniorb-12.title: Partial fractions and telescoping
nyciml-2021-22-spring-seniorb-12.body: $\dfrac{(-1)^n}{n(n+2)}=\dfrac{(-1)^n}{2}\!\left(\dfrac{1}{n}-\dfrac{1}{n+2}\right)$. Writing out terms, this nearly telescopes. The surviving terms after pairing are $\dfrac{1}{2}\!\left(-1+\dfrac{1}{2}+\dfrac{1}{99}-\dfrac{1}{100}\right)=\dfrac{1}{2}\cdot\dfrac{-4949}{9900}=\dfrac{-4949}{19800}$. **Answer: $-\dfrac{4949}{19800}$**

nyciml-2021-22-spring-seniorb-13.title: Pigeonhole on x-coordinates
nyciml-2021-22-spring-seniorb-13.body:
Every lattice point in the box has $x$-coordinate $0,1,2,3$ or $4$. A non-vertical line meets each vertical line $x=k$ at most once, so it contains at most one lattice point with each $x$-coordinate: at most $5$ lattice points.

The line $y=1$ passes through $(0,1),(1,1),(2,1),(3,1),(4,1)$, so $5$ is achieved.

**Answer: 5**

nyciml-2021-22-spring-seniorb-14.title: Space diagonal of cube
nyciml-2021-22-spring-seniorb-14.body: The space diagonal of the $5\times5\times5$ cube has length $5\sqrt{3}$. The center of the cube to any corner has distance $\tfrac{5\sqrt{3}}{2}$. For the central sphere (radius 2) to be tangent to a corner sphere (radius $r$): $r+2=\tfrac{5\sqrt{3}}{2}$, so $r=\dfrac{5\sqrt{3}-4}{2}$. **Answer: $\dfrac{5\sqrt{3}-4}{2}$**

nyciml-2021-22-spring-seniorb-16.title: Geometric series
nyciml-2021-22-spring-seniorb-16.body: Each shaded triangle $E_{i-1}D_iE_i$ has area $\tfrac{1}{4}$ of the sub-triangle it sits in. The first shaded triangle ($E_0D_1E_1$) has area $\tfrac{1}{4}[ABC]=\tfrac{1}{4}\cdot72=18$. Each subsequent shaded triangle is $\tfrac{1}{4}$ the previous. Total shaded area $=18\cdot\dfrac{1}{1-1/4}=18\cdot\dfrac{4}{3}=24$. **Answer: 24**

nyciml-2021-22-spring-seniorb-18.title: Casework on steps
nyciml-2021-22-spring-seniorb-18.body: Let Alice start at 0 and Bob at 1. After 5 steps each, we need Alice's position $=$ Bob's position $+1$. If Bob takes $n$ left-steps (net displacement $5-2n$) and Alice takes $n-1$ left-steps (net $7-2n$): Alice ends at $7-2n$, Bob ends at $1+(5-2n)=6-2n$. Difference: $(7-2n)-(6-2n)=1$ ✓. Number of ways: $\binom{5}{n}\binom{5}{n-1}$ for $n=1,\ldots,5$. By the Vandermonde-type identity $\sum_{n=0}^5\binom{5}{n}\binom{5}{n+1}=\binom{10}{4}=210$, the sum $\sum_{n=1}^5\binom{5}{n}\binom{5}{n-1}=210$. Total outcomes: $2^{10}=1024$. Probability $=\dfrac{210}{1024}=\dfrac{105}{512}$. **Answer: $\dfrac{105}{512}$**

nyciml-2021-22-spring-seniorb-20.title: Coordinates after 2.5 sides
nyciml-2021-22-spring-seniorb-20.body: Charles walks $5=2+2+1$ km: 2 full sides, then 1 km along the third. Each interior angle of a regular octagon is $135°$; the exterior angle is $45°$. From the starting vertex $A$, after 2 full sides: label vertices $A,B,C,...$ going in one direction; $A\to B$ has direction $0°$, $B\to C$ turns $45°$. After $AB$ and $BC$ he reaches $C$. The displacement: set $A=(0,0)$. $B=(2,0)$. Direction $AB$ is horizontal; at $B$ turn $45°$ counterclockwise: direction of $BC$ is $45°$. $C=B+(2\cos45°,2\sin45°)=(2+\sqrt{2},\sqrt{2})$. At $C$ turn $45°$: direction $CD$ is $90°$. Walk 1 km: reach $(2+\sqrt{2},\sqrt{2}+1)$. Distance from $A=(0,0)$: $\sqrt{(2+\sqrt{2})^2+(1+\sqrt{2})^2}=\sqrt{9+6\sqrt{2}}=\sqrt{6}+\sqrt{3}$ (since $(\sqrt{6}+\sqrt{3})^2=9+6\sqrt{2}$). **Answer: $\sqrt{6}+\sqrt{3}$**

nyciml-2021-22-spring-seniorb-23.title: Power of a point
nyciml-2021-22-spring-seniorb-23.body: Since both circles have radius 8 and are centered at $C$ and $D$ with $CD=8$, triangle $ECD$ has $EC=ED=CD=8$, making it equilateral. The height of an equilateral triangle with side 8 is $4\sqrt{3}$. Area $=\tfrac{1}{2}\cdot8\cdot4\sqrt{3}=16\sqrt{3}$. **Answer: $16\sqrt{3}$**

nyciml-2021-22-spring-seniorb-24.title: Bayes' theorem
nyciml-2021-22-spring-seniorb-24.body: $P(a+b+c=15\mid\text{odd})=\dfrac{P(a+b+c=15)}{P(\text{odd})}$. Number of triples with $a+b+c=15$: by stars-and-bars with $0\le a,b,c\le15$: $\binom{17}{2}=136$ (all solutions fit since max is 45). $P(a+b+c=15)=136/16^3$. $P(\text{odd})=1/2$. So the answer $=\dfrac{136/16^3}{1/2}=\dfrac{272}{16^3}=\dfrac{272}{4096}=\dfrac{17}{256}$. **Answer: $\dfrac{17}{256}$**

nyciml-2021-22-spring-seniorb-25.title: Fix one person
nyciml-2021-22-spring-seniorb-25.body:
Choose 3 of the 10 seats so that no two chosen seats are adjacent.

Fix one particular person $P$.
- If $P$ is chosen, his two neighbours are not; the other 2 chosen people come from the remaining 7 people in a row, no two adjacent: $\binom{7-2+1}{2}=\binom{6}{2}=15$ ways.
- If $P$ is not chosen, the 3 chosen people come from the other 9 people in a row, no two adjacent: $\binom{9-3+1}{3}=\binom{7}{3}=35$ ways.

Total: $15+35=50$.

**Answer: 50**

nyciml-2021-22-spring-seniorb-26.title: Conjugate pair sum is an integer
nyciml-2021-22-spring-seniorb-26.body: $(2+\sqrt{3})^6+(2-\sqrt{3})^6$ is an integer (odd powers of $\sqrt{3}$ cancel). $(2-\sqrt{3})\approx0.27$, so $(2-\sqrt{3})^6<1$. Computing: $2[(2^6+\binom{6}{2}2^4\cdot3+\binom{6}{4}2^2\cdot3^2+3^3)]=2[64+720+540+27]=2\cdot1351=2702$. So $(2+\sqrt{3})^6=2702-(2-\sqrt{3})^6$, which is slightly less than 2702. The largest integer below it is $2701$. **Answer: 2701**
